title: Arriving in Chicago and meeting its musicians
summary: He knows Budd Johnson and Jesse Stone and meets Jimmie Noone, Earl Hines and others.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But when I got to Chicago I knew a lot of people. Budd Johnson was there and other jazz musicians, you know, because they didn't all stay in the same place, they'd move around. So I knew Jesse Stone...oh, Jesse Stone was in Kansas City. Do you know about him?
He was a fine arranger, wasn't he?
And piano player. He was a good arranger, yeah. But Jesse was in Chicago and then, I knew a lot of other people. I knew a guy named Eddie Torrenti who was an old friend of
mine and then he was a friend of Valetta's. And then I met Jimmie Noone and then I met Earl Hines, Barney Bigard, Omer Simeon...Who was playing the drums for Earl Hines then? He lived in...ah....
Walter Bishop. Yeah, I heard you. Was it Walter Bishop or was it....mmmh...
It was somebody before him...Earl's band...

I think it was Walter Bishop. But anyway you...and then I began to see where the Peking Restaurant was and seeing Louis and Teddy Wilson...In other words, I was like a person that had started in kindergarten with that man with that twenty-five cents and that woman saying this, and Mrs. Ella B. Moore saying this, and going on to those little road shows when I met Oscar Peterson.
